problem: Existing VLN VLA models are tightly coupled end-to-end systems that map vision-language input to short-horizon discrete actions (e.g. forward 0.25 m). This gives fragmented motion, high latency from frequent large-VLM calls, and poor dynamic obstacle avoidance.
motivation: Real-world deployment needs smooth, real-time control and agile local decisions, while a VLM's generalization should be kept for long-horizon reasoning. Separating slow global grounding from fast local control lets each level specialize and lets the two run at different frequencies.
key_idea: A dual-system VLN model in which a VLM (System 2, 2 Hz) grounds a mid-term pixel goal and passes it, together with latent-query features, to a lightweight diffusion transformer (System 1, 30 Hz) that generates smooth trajectories from high-frequency RGB.
insight: Decoupled sequential training (train System 2 on pixel-goal grounding, freeze it, then train latent queries and the DiT) preserves VLM generalization; joint one-stage training converges slower and hurts System 2. Both goal types matter: removing the pixel goal from context, or replacing latent queries with frozen hidden states, degrades performance. Replacing System 1 with point-goal planners (iPlanner, NavDP), even with oracle depth, is worse on VLN-PE, because System 1 tolerates small pixel-goal errors while point-goal projection is sensitive to them. System 1 saturates with about 10% of the data.
method: Farthest pixel goal grounding: Qwen-VL-2.5 7B takes egocentric RGB history plus the instruction and outputs 2D pixel coordinates of the farthest visible future waypoint. Training labels come from projecting the 3D VLN-CE trajectory into the image, with depth-based occlusion filtering.
Self-directed view adjustment: System 2 can output Turn Left/Right 15° or Look Up/Down 15° actions (up to 4 consecutive turns) before predicting the pixel goal, and outputs STOP at the end.

Latent goal representation: four learnable latent queries (<TRAJ> tokens) are appended after the pixel-goal text and processed by the frozen VLM. Their final-layer hidden states (3584 projected to 768) are the latent goal, trained by prompt tuning.

Multi-modal conditioning DiT (System 1): a small DiT (hidden 384, 12 layers, 6 heads) generates 32 dense waypoints with a flow-matching loss. It is conditioned on the latent goal and on fused RGB features of the System-2 frame and the current frame, from a DepthAnythingV2-S ViT, self-attention, and a Q-Former compressing to 32 tokens.

Asynchronous inference: System 2 runs slowly, its latent goal stays fixed, and System 1 updates trajectories at high frequency from fresh RGB. KV-cache reuse cuts System 2 trajectory inference from 1.1 s to 0.7 s, and System 1 takes 0.03 s with TensorRT.

Two-stage decoupled training: Stage 1 fully fine-tunes Qwen2.5-VL (StreamVLN data recipe, 1 epoch, 14k steps, lr 2e-5). Stage 2 freezes the VLM and trains only the latent queries and DiT (15k steps, lr 1e-4, only pixel-goal samples).

Social-VLN benchmark: R2R-CE extended with Habitat 3.0 humanoids placed along GT trajectories, plus a Human Collision Rate (HCR) metric. A 763K-episode social-navigation training set was collected across 60 MP3D scenes.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-7B (fine-tuned, System 2) + small DiT diffusion policy with DepthAnythingV2-S ViT encoder (System 1)
setting.training_data: VLN-CE trajectories following the StreamVLN data recipe for System 2 (pixel-goal, view-adjustment and STOP samples); System 1 uses the pixel-goal samples; 763K Social-VLN obstacle-avoidance episodes were collected. Not fine-tuned on VLN-PE trajectories.
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB (history frames plus high-frequency current RGB); RGB-D is streamed in the real world for odometry/trajectory transformation
setting.action_space: System 2: discrete view adjustments (turn/look 15°) and pixel goals; System 1: continuous trajectories of 32 waypoints tracked by an MPC controller
setting.simulator: Habitat (VLN-CE, Social-VLN with Habitat 3.0 humanoids) and Isaac Sim (VLN-PE)
setting.privileged: none (oracle depth used only in the point-goal planner ablation)

numbers_note: Real-world results (SR/NE over 20 trials per scenario) and the goal-conditioning and data-scaling ablations are given only in figures.
results: DualVLN reaches 64.3 SR / 58.5 SPL on R2R-CE val-unseen and 61.4 SR / 51.8 SPL on RxR-CE, using only monocular RGB and beating StreamVLN (56.9/51.9 and 52.9/46.0). On VLN-PE it reaches 51.60 SR zero-shot versus NaVid 22.42 and RDP 25.24. On Social-VLN it beats StreamVLN (SR 37.2 vs 31.4), but HCR stays high (35.4).
limitations: Social-VLN performance drops sharply (about 27% SR) and human collision rate stays high, leaving large room for improvement.
System 1 is robust only to small pixel-goal errors; large or semantically wrong pixel goals, especially near obstacles, lead to failure.
The model requires a remote GPU server (about 20GB, RTX 4090), and System 2 inference still takes about 0.7 s.
